title: Bounded-Scope Contingency Protocol for Cycle Overruns
creator: Avery Chen
description: Create a practical, prescriptive playbook that product, eng, and design can use mid-cycle when capacity signals show a >15% drop in deliverable throughput or a major unplanned blocker emerges. The playbook defines: 1) detection signals and owner handoffs, 2) a bounded scope reduction algorithm for feature tranches, 3) staffing rotation and surge hedges, and 4) communication templates for stakeholders and cross-functional teams. This ticket captures the PRD, decision criteria, run-of-show for a 48h rapid-triage, and rollout plan for the playbook across product squads.
acceptance_criteria: A concise 2-page playbook doc published in Drive with runbook scripts and templates
Automated detection thresholds added to the cycle dashboard that trigger the '48h rapid-triage' alert
Three canonical scope-trim patterns (vertical slice, deferral, de-scope acceptance criteria) documented with examples
Staffing rotation protocol with surge pool nomination and handoff checklist documented
Signoff from ENG PM and Design leads and a dry-run completed with one squad
decision_log: 2026-02-27: Decided to use a hybrid approach for scope cuts — tranche-based with a max 30% surface-area reduction per tranche to avoid regressions to core UX
2026-03-03: Agreed on detection signal thresholds: sustained >15% slip in cycle throughput for 3 consecutive business days OR a P0 blocker affecting >2 teams
2026-03-05: Chose to prioritize skills-agnostic surge pool over deep-specialist reassignments to minimize onboarding cost during surge
2026-03-10: Opted for a default rollback window of 7 days post-surge to evaluate customer metrics before reintroducing deferred scope

2026-03-04: Engineering review: recommended adding KV-cache and inference rollout exceptions for runtime-critical work (Eleanor Yu)
